cards.text: Isaiah son of Amoz, who saw a vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem, is looking ahead to a day that's coming. He says that in that day, a song will be sung in the land of Judah. And the first thing the singers talk about is their strong city.

cards.question: In the song Judah will sing, salvation is what makes up the strong city's walls and ramparts.

cards.text: Next line: open the gates, somebody's coming in. Friend, the last thing that opened up for me was the front of a junk drawer, so I get VERY excited about gates.

cards.question: The song calls for the gates to open so a righteous nation may enter, one that remains ___.

cards.text: Then the song makes a promise: God will keep the steadfast of mind in perfect peace. PERFECT peace, baker, and I spent years in a drawer next to dead batteries arguing all night about who had the most charge left.

cards.question: Why does God keep the steadfast of mind in perfect peace?

cards.text: Then the song says GOD the LORD is the Rock eternal. ETERNAL, baker, and I went blurry after a few years of birthday batches.

cards.question: Because GOD the LORD is the Rock eternal, the song says to trust in the LORD ___.

cards.text: Then the song says God has humbled those who dwell on high. And He lays the lofty city low, all the way down into the dust.

cards.question: The lofty city is lying in the dust. Whose feet trample it down?

cards.text: Now the song says the path of the righteous is level, and God clears a straight path for the upright. Baker, my whole planet is ONE bakery big, and I still take wrong turns.

cards.question: As they walk in the path of God's judgments, the singers say they wait for the LORD.
The singers are waiting for the LORD. What do they say is the desire of their souls?

cards.text: Then the singer gets personal: "My soul longs for You in the night; indeed, my spirit seeks You at dawn." Night AND dawn, baker, before the snooze button even gets a vote.

cards.question: The singer says something happens when God's judgments come upon the earth. What is it?

answers.text: The people of the world learn righteousness
The mountains of the world melt like wax
The rivers of the world turn to blood

cards.question: The song says that when grace is shown to the wicked man, he learns righteousness too.

cards.text: He's right there in the land of righteousness, acting unjustly, and he fails to see the majesty of the LORD. That's a man standing in the middle of a bakery asking where the cookies are.

cards.question: Right after the wicked man, the song says God's hand is upraised, but they do not see it. What does the song say they will see?

cards.text: They'll see it and be put to shame. And the song says the fire set for God's enemies will consume them.
Then the singers say, "O LORD, You will establish peace for us." And they pull out the list of everything they've ever gotten done, like it's performance review season.

cards.question: Looking back at all they've accomplished, the singers say the ___ has done it for them.
Other lords besides God have ruled over the singers. Even so, they say they confess the LORD's name alone.

cards.text: Then the song says, "The dead will not live; the departed spirits will not rise." God has punished and destroyed them and wiped out ALL memory of them, which is more forgotten than me, and I spent years behind the takeout menus in a junk drawer.

cards.question: Then the song turns to God's own nation, and the singers say twice that He has enlarged it. What does the song say He has extended?

answers.text: All the borders of the land
All the days of their kings

cards.text: Then the song remembers the hard times: when God disciplined them, they sought Him in their distress. Baker, NOTHING gets me looking for help faster than a smoking oven.

cards.question: In their distress, when God disciplined them, what did they pour out?

cards.text: Then the singers paint a picture of themselves: like a woman about to give birth, writhing and crying out in pain in the LORD's presence. I'm a cookie stamper, friend, so I am NOT about to pretend I know that kind of pain.

cards.question: The singers felt like a woman about to give birth. After all that pain, what did they give birth to?

cards.text: All that pain and it's WIND, with no salvation given to the earth and no life brought into the world. That's me in my worn-out days, pressing down HARD on the dough and lifting up a blur.
But hold on, baker, because the song turns right here. Now it talks to God about "Your dead."

cards.question: The song says "Your dead" will stay in the dust.

cards.text: The song says, "Your dead will live; their bodies will rise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust!" Friend, I lay in the dust of a junk drawer for YEARS, and that line makes me hop my whole gold base around the bakery.
Then the song adds a picture: your dew is like the dew of the morning.

cards.question: Those who dwell in the dust are told to awake and sing. What does the song say the earth will bring forth?

cards.text: Then a call goes out: "Go, my people, enter your rooms and shut your doors behind you. Hide yourselves a little while until the wrath has passed."

cards.question: Why hide? Because the LORD is coming out of His dwelling to ___ the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity.
When the LORD comes out of His dwelling, the earth will keep concealing her slain.

cards.text: Then in that day, the LORD takes His sharp, great and mighty sword. He brings judgment on Leviathan, the fleeing serpent, the coiling serpent.

cards.question: The LORD has His sword out against Leviathan. He will ___ the dragon of the sea.

findings.problem: The people in distress are referred to only as "their," "them" and "they." The question never identifies them as the singers or God's people, so it depends on an earlier card to establish who is being discussed.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the quotation contains two sentences, and Papa Dorin then adds another sentence about the junk drawer and hopping around the bakery.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
